chunks: Marry off those who are single among you, and those of your male and female servants who are righteous. If they are poor, God will enrich them of His grace, for God is bounteous and all-knowing.

key_terms.الْأَيَامَىٰ: Plural of daym, referring to unmarried men or women

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about marrying off the poor and single?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to encourage the social integration of slaves and servants through marriage, highlighting the spiritual merit of freeing them as a consequence of marital stability. The promise of divine enrichment (غنا) is interpreted not merely as material wealth but as sufficiency in contentment and ability to fulfill marital duties, reflecting God's vast knowledge of individual circumstances.
